questions.q: In which land did Job live?
questions.evidence: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job

questions.q: How many sons were born to Job?
questions.evidence: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters

questions.q: "Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away." How did Job end that saying?
With what did Satan strike Job from the sole of his foot to his head?
questions.evidence: So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head

questions.q: Who told Job, "Renounce God, and die"?
questions.evidence: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die

questions.q: Which of Job's friends was called the Temanite?
questions.evidence: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite

questions.q: How long did the friends sit with Job on the ground, without a word?
questions.evidence: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great

questions.q: "I know that my" who "lives", Job said?
questions.evidence: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives

questions.q: Which young man spoke after the three friends fell silent?
questions.evidence: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job

questions.q: Out of what did Yahweh answer Job?
questions.evidence: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind

questions.q: "Where were you when I laid the foundations of" what, Yahweh asked?
questions.evidence: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth

questions.q: How much did Yahweh give Job, compared with what he had before?
questions.evidence: Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before

questions.q: How long did Job live after this?
questions.evidence: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations
